summary.identity: Odisha Board of Revenue (BOR) Case Management System — Cuttack. Header banner reads 'BOR cuttack'. NOT a property-record portal.
summary.verdictReason: Result table exposes ONLY case-management columns (SL NO, Section, Case No, Court Name, Petitioner Name, Opposite Party Name). No plot/khata/village/mouza/tehsil column appears in any of the 4 working search forms. The 'Hal Khata No.' and 'Hal Plot No.' search options exist as form inputs but are KEYS to look up revenue cases — they do not cause the result table to display plot/khata/village details. This is the wrong system for ClearDeed's need to match court cases BACK to a plot/khata/village.
summary.coreFinding: ccms.nic.in can answer: 'Is there an Odisha revenue court case for hal-khata 415 in Khordha?' It cannot answer: 'On plot 415 / khata 94 / village Mendhasala, which revenue court cases are pending?' The first question is forward-only; the second question — which ClearDeed needs — is reverse-lookup and the result table does not echo back the plot/khata key.

killCriteria.reason: ccms.nic.in is the Odisha Board of Revenue Case Management System — a case-search portal, not a property-record portal. Although the form offers 'Hal Khata No.' and 'Hal Plot No.' search keys, the result table does not echo the plot/khata/village. ClearDeed's need is REVERSE LOOKUP (given a plot/khata/village, list all revenue cases touching it). This portal is FORWARD LOOKUP (given a hal-khata, list cases filed against that khata) — and even then the result columns don't include the khata/village of the cases listed.

whatItAnswers: Is there a Board of Revenue case filed against hal-khata 415 of mouza Mendhasala?
Is there an OSS Act 15(B) case pending against petitioner X in court Y in year 2024?
whatItDoesNotAnswer: List all revenue cases touching plot 415 (regardless of khata).
Match a person's name to revenue cases linked to a specific village or mouza.
Show whether a court case is connected to a BDA-zone property.
usefulForClearDeed.potentialManualUse: A user with a hal-khata number (from Bhulekh) CAN query ccms.nic.in to see if there is a pending revenue case. This is a useful manual-verification step for buyers — but it requires the buyer to have a hal-khata, not just GPS or plot number.

anomalies: Root URL `/` does an immediate meta-refresh to `/loginHome.html`. There is no public landing page.
JSESSIONID is set on `/loginHome.html` and required across all subsequent requests — without it, /searchCases.html returns the captcha but POSTs may bounce.
casetypeId dropdown has ~409 options but only ~16 unique values (repeated per court). Server-side bug; not a fetcher blocker.

Result table for /findCase.html is populated by JavaScript (table id=hearingdetailsstatus). Static HTML shows 'Sorry,case number Not Found' only; column schema is rendered by JS based on response payload. We did not capture a populated case for schema confirmation.

Hal-Khata search uses a maxlength=10 numeric-style input (onKeyPress=checkValidate). Hal khata numbers in Bhulekh typically follow patterns like '415' or '415/1' — 10 chars is enough. Copy/paste is blocked on the client.
The 'Search By Case Registration ID/ Case Number/ Petitioner Name/ Hal Plot No./ Hal Kahta No.' panel header says 'Kahta' (a misspelling of Khata) — typo in the live portal.

Captcha image is served from /captcha.jpg with no cache-busting query string — image may be cached client-side and re-presented to the user even though server expects a fresh value. Stale-captcha is a likely failure mode for naive fetcher implementations.
nextSteps: DO NOT build a fetcher for ccms.nic.in. It is not the right system for property-keyed revenue-court coverage.

Keep ccms.nic.in as a MANUAL VERIFICATION step in the report's 'What to Ask Next' panel. The buyer already has a hal-khata from Bhulekh — instruct them to query ccms.nic.in/searchCases.html (Hal Khata No. option) to check for cases, instead of building automated coverage.
If reverse-lookup (plot → cases) is needed in the future, the right source is the eCourts party-name search with plot/khata cross-reference done by a human investigator — not ccms.nic.in.

If automated coverage of ccms.nic.in is later required (e.g., for hal-khata-driven bulk checks in T-031 follow-up), the captcha is solvable at >90% confidence with tesseract.js. The blocker is not captcha; it is the missing reverse-lookup result schema.

Confirm with the founder whether 'court cases on this property' was actually expected from ccms.nic.in or whether the original RCCMS brief (T-011) referred to a different portal. The current Bhubaneswar revenue-court data needs a different source — possibly Bhulekh Back Page mutation references (which already provide title-chain anchors), or a paid concierge service via the Board of Revenue office.
